subtitle: A whole clause before the noun, and four ways to say it can be done
words.intro: In Papenburg, far inland, a shipyard builds the largest cruise ships in the world. Each one is too big for the river. So the river is dammed, dredged and closed, and the whole region comes to watch.
words.more: Auch auf der Werft · also at the shipyard
words.groups[0].title: Die Werft · the shipyard
words.groups[1].title: Geht das? · can it be done?

grammar[0].fact: Mark Twain said that when a German dives into a sentence, you won’t see him again until he comes up on the other side, with his verb in his mouth. Folded phrases like these are what he had in mind. Newspapers use them to save space.

grammar[1].blocks[1].title: ist zu … : can or must?
grammar[1].blocks[1].root.q: Is there leicht, schwer or kaum?
grammar[1].blocks[2].title: -bar and -lich
grammar[1].blocks[2].note: Not verstehbar: learn each one as a word.
grammar[1].blocks[3].title: Words for the practice page
grammar[1].fact: Watch out for *ist zu*: *Die Tür ist zu schließen* means the door must be closed. *Das Problem ist zu lösen* means it can be solved. Only the context will tell you, and in the army, the context is a sergeant.

opener.caption: In der Halle der Werft: Hier wird das Schiff Stück für Stück zusammengebaut.
document.intro: A real old signboard of the same shipyard. It’s all compound nouns, in handwriting. Take them apart: *die Maschine + die Fabrik*, *das Eisen + die Gießerei*, *der Kessel + die Schmiede*.
document.fact: The family firm has been building ships in Papenburg since 1795, first of wood, then of iron. A shipyard that far from the sea makes little sense, and it’s a very big employer.
document.tasks[0].instruction: Write the two words each one is made of.
document.tasks[2].instruction: Say each one with sich lassen.
reading.intro: A new ship is to leave the yard on Saturday. Maya’s friend Jan is the project manager, and he reads a note aloud in the canteen. It’s from head office, in the style head office uses.
reading.photos[1].caption: Das in der Halle gebaute Schiff, kurz vor dem Ende.
reading.fact: The Meyer shipyard in Papenburg lies far inland, up the river Ems. Each new ship must be taken downriver, stern first, and a barrier is closed to raise the water. Thousands line the banks to watch.
reading.tasks[1].instruction: Unfold each phrase into a relative clause.
